fabric-api-base.reason: Shipped by Fabricated (vendored from upstream); every Fabric API module builds on it, the native ones too. Its package net.fabricmc.fabric.api.util is split with fabric-content-registries-v0, whose two interfaces there (Block2ObjectMap, Item2ObjectMap) Fabricated ships with it, as the in-game mod's packages are taken out of Fabric jars.

fabric-biome-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API and biome source mixins, with biome modifications applied as a Forge biome modifier. Upstream's access widener opens the biome's climate field, which Forge's coremod needs private to point reads of a biome's climate and effects at its modified info, so with the module passed through the coremod failed and no biome modifier's climate or effects reached the game; upstream's modifications also replace biome fields Forge no longer reads.

fabric-dimensions-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API and its teleport target hook. Forge 47 moved vanilla's dimension change, whose reads of the End's key upstream's hook redirected, into its changeDimension with a teleporter and a lambda that teleporter calls, so passed through the module failed pre-flight: a Fabric teleport now hands Forge's dimension change a teleporter that asks for no portal and isn't vanilla's, which leaves out the End's obsidian platform and a player's credits on leaving the End, as upstream does. Upstream's codec hook (RegistryCodecsMixin), which makes the dimensions in level.dat skip one that no longer decodes, is not shipped: Forge 47 replaces the same map codec with its own lenient one (its fix for MC-197860), keeping the entries that decode. Nor are upstream's DataFixerUpper mixins (Schema2832Mixin, TaggedChoiceMixin, TaggedChoiceTypeMixin): Forge 47 loads DataFixerUpper without mixin support. Lost: upgrading a world whose dimensions use a chunk generator type no installed mod registers fails in DataFixerUpper as it does without Fabric API (UNVERIFIED whether Forge's own handling covers it).

fabric-entity-events-v1.reason: Forge's LivingEntity asks the bed's state (BlockState.setBedOccupied, getBedDirection) where vanilla sets the occupied property and asks BedBlock, which upstream's occupation and sleeping direction hooks look for, so pre-flight left them out: SET_BED_OCCUPATION_STATE and MODIFY_SLEEPING_DIRECTION never ran, and the red bed upstream's ALLOW_BED hook stands in for an admitted block in startSleeping reached Forge's setBedOccupied, which set a red bed in the world in the block's place. Fabricated's in-game mod runs both events at Forge's calls and sets the occupied state of the block that is there (SLEEP-1, as on Forge 61 to 66).

fabric-events-interaction-v0.reason: Forge's destroyBlock no longer calls Block.playerWillDestroy and Block.destroy itself, where upstream's hooks fire PlayerBlockBreakEvents.BEFORE and AFTER: both moved into a private removeBlock Forge added, so the two hooks found nothing to apply to (pre-flight only warned, as they capture locals) and the events never ran when a player broke a block. Fabricated's in-game mod fires them at the same points of Forge's method instead, BEFORE (with CANCELED when refused) once the game's checks pass and AFTER once removeBlock removed the block, before the drops (BREAK-1, as on Forge 61 to 66).

fabric-loot-api-v2.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API and builder mixins. Forge 47 keeps a loot table's pools in a list, which upstream's accessor and table copy read as an array, so passed through the module failed pre-flight. The loot table events run from Fabricated's hook on the loot data manager's apply, as vanilla receives the parsed tables (after Forge's loot table event), and a table's source is decided from Forge's packs (mods' data is built in) instead of fabric-resource-loader-v0's.

fabric-loot-tables-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's deprecated API over fabric-loot-api-v2's events, its initializer run by the in-game mod. Its loot table mixin read the pools as an array, which Forge 47 keeps in a list (passed through, pre-flight disabled it), and Forge's own public LootPool.getRolls() implements its pool getter of the same name.

fabric-particles-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API, its hook that registers Fabric's particle factories once vanilla's are in, and its block dust tint event, asked where Forge 47 decides the tint (its block extensions' areBreakingParticlesTinted replaced vanilla's grass check, which upstream's hook looked for). Forge 47 keeps the particle engine's factories in a map by the type's id, which upstream's accessor read as a map by raw id, so passed through the module failed pre-flight on the client and Fabric mods' particles had no factories: Fabric's factories and their sprite sets are registered through the engine's own methods, where Forge registers its mods' (PART-1).

fabric-registry-sync-v0.reason: Forge 47 loads the data pack registries from its own list, which upstream's mixin replaced with vanilla's and the Fabric mods', losing Forge's biome and structure modifiers: Fabricated adds the Fabric mods' dynamic registries to Forge's list instead.

fabric-rendering-v1.reason: Forge 47 keeps block and item colour providers in maps by registry holder under the names of vanilla's IdMappers by id, which upstream's colour provider lookups shadow (in SRG's names here): Fabricated's in-game mod looks providers up in Forge's maps instead of upstream's methods (COLOR-1). Forge 47 also resolves a core shader program's namespace, and its stages' and imports' (ShaderInstance's constructor by ResourceLocation, ForgeHooksClient.getShaderImportLocation), where upstream's shader mixins rewrite the same names for Fabric's shader programs: applied on top of Forge's, the stage rewrite doubled the namespace (forge:forge:shaders/core/...), and the client stopped at its first resource reload. Fabric's namespaced shader programs load through Forge's resolution instead.

fabric-tag-api-v1.reason: Forge 47's tag files already have a remove list, which its tag loader applies, and upstream's FabricTagFile.remove() reads it: upstream's own list conflicts with Forge's, and its tag loader hooks, which apply that list, are left out with it. Tag files' fabric:remove entries are not read on Forge 47 yet; Forge's remove entries are.
